Good web design Fort Worth Texas owners can be proud of starts with a simple fact: Fort Worth is not a suburb of anywhere. It has its own downtown, its own history and its own customers, and the people searching for a roofer, a cafe or a bookkeeper there tend to type "Fort Worth", or the name of their part of town, rather than "DFW". A site that files you under the whole Metroplex makes those searchers work harder to figure out whether you are close.

Dominion Web Design Pro builds sites that say where you are. Maurice Johnson, a Texan working from Big Sandy in East Texas, writes every page by hand, you see a free demo before any invoice, and the price is printed: $497, $997 or $1,997, one time.

A city of a million that still gets called "the other half"

Fort Worth crossed a line most Texans did not expect it to cross so soon. The city reports a population of 1,008,106 as of July 1, 2024, the first time it reached a million, and it gained 23,442 residents in that single year. Newer Census figures reported by NBC DFW put it at about 1.03 million and tenth among U.S. cities. That is bigger than many state capitals, and yet outsiders still talk about it as the western end of Dallas.

Locals do not. Fort Worth has a western identity it has kept on purpose, along with neighborhoods and districts that each pull their own crowd. For a small business, that pride is useful. A customer who thinks of themselves as a Fort Worth person, or a Near Southside person, notices when a website talks to them in those terms, and notices just as quickly when it does not.

Web design Fort Worth, Texas customers recognize, district by district

The same plumber or caterer might work all over the city, but a shop with a storefront lives in one place. Here is what visitors to a few of Fort Worth's best known areas tend to need from a small business site.

AreaWhat is true thereWhat your site should cover
Stockyards National Historic DistrictThe Fort Worth Herd drives longhorns down East Exchange Avenue twice a day, at 11:30 a.m. and 4:00 p.m., so visitors plan around set times.Hours that match the crowd, walking distance from the Livestock Exchange Building, parking, and whether to book ahead.
Near Southside and Magnolia AvenueA historic mixed-use district just south of downtown, with Magnolia as its main street and new independent shops, restaurants and bars opening every year. Fort Worth South, Inc. counts it as the second largest employment center in Tarrant County.A menu or service list as real text, the cross street, and a reason to visit that a chain down the road cannot claim.
Cultural District, West 7th and Camp BowieWest 7th Street crosses University Drive and becomes the brick-paved Camp Bowie Boulevard, near the Kimbell, the Modern and the Amon Carter museums. The Camp Bowie District runs out to Loop 820.Which stretch you are on, since Camp Bowie is long, plus nearby landmarks people already know.
Far north Fort Worth and AllianceTexasHillwood's 27,000-acre AllianceTexas development reports more than 574 companies, with related projects reaching Haslet, Roanoke, Northlake and Westlake.The towns you cover by name, since many north side addresses read as a suburb, not as Fort Worth.

The TCU area, the east side and the neighborhoods south of I-20 have their own customers too. The point is not to list every name. It is to pick the ones your buyers use and write about them honestly.

Fort Worth website design that does not hide you in the Metroplex

Google explains its local results with three ideas: relevance, which is how well a listing matches the search; distance from the searcher or the place named; and prominence, which is how well known a business is. When someone types "electrician Camp Bowie" or "fort worth website design", the place name is doing a lot of the work. A site that mentions Fort Worth once, in the footer, gives Google little to match.

So we put the city and the parts of it you serve where they belong: the page title, the first paragraph, the service area page and the contact page, all in plain sentences. Nobody can promise a ranking, and we will not. What we can do is make the site clearly about Fort Worth work.

Web development in Fort Worth, explained without the jargon

About 260 people a month search for web development in Fort Worth. Some need a programmer. Most need a working small business site and are not sure which word to use.

What we build

Hand-written pages that load fast on a phone, a contact form that emails you every lead, page titles, descriptions and a sitemap sent to Google, and schema markup on Pro and Agency. We design it, write it, code it and host it, and you own it outright.

What needs a different firm

Online stores and custom software are not in our packages. If you need a booking system tied to your own database, a parts catalog with thousands of items or a customer login area, hire a development shop for that, and we will say so before you buy anything from us.

Comparing a web design company in Fort Worth? Put the numbers side by side

A fair comparison needs the whole picture: what you pay up front, what you pay each month and who owns the site if you leave. Here is ours in one paragraph. Starter is $497 for five pages and goes live in 7 to 14 days. Pro is $997 and adds a photo gallery, ten city pages, Google Business Profile setup and an AI chat widget that is free for 14 days, then $297 a month. Agency is $1,997 and adds keyword research, a page for every town and service pair worth having, and setup of an AI phone agent; the agent is free for 7 days, then $297 a month for up to 750 minutes, cancel any time, and it is not part of the one-time price. Hosting, maintenance and updates are included while you keep the AI agent, or $49 a month without it.

We do not sell page counts. A shop on Magnolia may need five strong pages, and a pressure washing company working from Benbrook to Keller may need thirty. Either way, each page has to earn its place.

Where Fort Worth owners can get free or low-cost help

A website is one tool. These local programs help with the rest, from business plans to city contracts:

  • Devoyd Jennings Business Assistance CenterRun by the City of Fort Worth on the James E. Guinn Entrepreneurial Campus, with training, technical assistance and leads on funding for startups and established firms.
  • Small Business Development ProgramThe city's program, run with the Fort Worth Chamber, the Fort Worth Hispanic Chamber and the Fort Worth Metropolitan Black Chamber under a contract that began in September 2025. The Hispanic Chamber offers help in Spanish; the Black Chamber runs bonding and insurance workshops.
  • Tarrant Small Business Development CenterHosted by Tarrant County College and part of the North Texas SBDC network, offering free one-on-one advising and low-cost workshops for Tarrant County owners.

Texas has about 3.52 million small businesses, firms with fewer than 500 employees, according to the SBA Office of Advocacy's 2025 profile. Plenty of them are competing for the same Fort Worth searches you are.

Common questions

How much do web designers charge for a website in Fort Worth?

Quotes vary widely, and many firms only give a number after a discovery call. Ask any designer for the full first-year cost in writing: the build, hosting, any monthly plan and what changes cost later. Our prices are printed. Starter is $497 for a five-page site, Pro is $997 for ten pages plus ten city pages, and Agency is $1,997 for a page for every town and service pair the keyword research supports, all paid once. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep the AI agent.

Should my website say Fort Worth or DFW?

Say Fort Worth, and then say where in Fort Worth. People type the place they mean: a neighborhood, a district, a suburb. "DFW" is a label for the whole region and covers Dallas, Arlington and dozens of other cities, so it tells a searcher and Google very little about where you actually work. If you serve towns outside the city limits too, give each one its own honest page instead of a list of names.

What is the difference between web design and web development in Fort Worth?

Design is what a visitor sees and reads: the layout, the words, the photos and the path to calling you. Development is the code underneath that makes it load, send form leads and stay online. A small business site needs both done well, and we do both for the sites in our packages. Custom software, like a customer portal or an online store with a large catalog, is a bigger development job that our packages do not cover, and we will tell you so up front.

Is there a web design company in Fort Worth that will show me the site before I pay?

We do that, though we are not in Fort Worth. Dominion Web Design Pro builds a free demo for your business first, and you decide after seeing it. Maurice Johnson writes and builds every site from Big Sandy in East Texas, so you deal with him by phone, email and shared links rather than in an office on West 7th.

Can you write pages for Fort Worth suburbs like Haslet or Benbrook?

Yes, for any town you really serve. Pro includes ten city pages, each researched and written for that place. Agency starts with keyword research across your whole service area and then writes a page for each town and service pair worth having, delivered in waves with the first live inside two weeks.

See your website before you pay for it

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
